title: [AUTHORED — condensed from the real export.pick pattern, same repo] OPENSEQ/WRITESEQ tab-delimited export, distinct from hashed-file access
sourceContent:
* condensed from zelenko/pick's export.pick CREATE1: paragraph
PGM = 'VZ.EXPORT.SAMPLE'
Z = CHAR(9)
FILE.ID = 'product_general.txt'
OPENSEQ 'MSG-OUT', FILE.ID TO OUT.FILE;
   ELSE CREATE OUT.FILE ELSE PRINT 'ERR: cannot create export file'
OPEN 'PRODUCT' TO KEYS ELSE STOP

EXECUTE 'SELECT PRODUCT WITH PRICE_LINE # "--11"'
LOOP
   READNEXT ID ELSE EXIT
   READV DESC FROM KEYS, ID, 1 ELSE DESC = ''
   CONVERT VM TO ' ' IN DESC
   LINE = ID:Z:DESC
   WRITESEQ LINE TO OUT.FILE ELSE CONTINUE
REPEAT
CLOSESEQ OUT.FILE ON ERROR PRINT 'ERROR CLOSING SEQ FILE'
RETURN
notes: AUTHORED — condensed from the real export.pick file's CREATE1: paragraph (same github.com/zelenko/pick repo, same attribution/license note as the other real entries) to keep this golden entry a clean single-claim example rather than the full 274-line file. Demonstrates the sequential-file-I/O access model (OPENSEQ/WRITESEQ/CLOSESEQ against a tab-delimited flat file) as genuinely distinct from the hashed-file READV/WRITEV world exercised in the other entries, plus a CONVERT VM TO ' ' flattening a multivalue field for export.
